properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 25 at 3:10PM MDT until July 25 at 3:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
Heavy rain has ended over the warned area. If flooding has been
observed...Please report it to your local law enforcement agency.
Flooding is no longer expected to pose a threat. Please continue to
heed remaining road closures.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 25 at 2:31PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 231 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
southern Castle Pines, or 20 miles south of Denver, moving east at 10
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 55 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Eastern Highlands Ranch, Castle Rock, Parker, Lone Tree, The
Pinery, Franktown, Castle Pines and Ponderosa Park.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 25 at 12:59PM MDT until July 25 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Ferris Burn Scar in...
Northwestern Dolores County in southwestern Colorado...
North Central Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
Southwestern San Miguel County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 400 PM MDT.

* At 1259 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Ferris Burn Scar. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flows.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around the Ferris Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around
the Ferris Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
mainly rural areas of Northwestern Dolores, North Central
Montezuma and Southwestern San Miguel Counties
properties.areaDesc: Dolores, CO; Montezuma, CO; San Miguel, CO

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 25 at 12:59PM MDT until July 25 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Lee and PL Gulch burn scar in...
Central Rio Blanco County in northwestern Colorado...

* Until 400 PM MDT.

* At 1259 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Lee and PL Gulch burn scars. Between 0.2 and
0.5 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to
3 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

Excessive rainfall will result in debris flow moving through the Lee
and PL Gulch burn scars. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around the Lee and PL
Gulch burn scars.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around
the Lee and PL Gulch burn scars.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lee and PL Gulch burn scars
